newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas rises on weather, output cuts.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas rises on weather, output cuts.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices edged higher Thursday, triggered by colder weather forecasts in the West and production cuts at a British Columbia gas processing plant, market sources said.

The Sumas, Washington market was rocked again today by news that Westcoast Energy would be cutting about 25 percent of production, or about 170 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd), at its McMahon gas plant in B.C.

The production cuts, expected to last through the weekend, pushed prices at the export point into the $1.20-1.25 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) range, from the $1.06-1.10 area earlier in the day.
March prices at Sumas were talked in the $1.06-1.10 per mmBtu range, down more than a $1 from February's index.
At the AECO storage hub, prices for Friday delivery climbed into the low-C$1.60s per gigajoule (GJ), up about 10 cents from Wednesday.
"We're still not maxing storage, but it's going to get a little cooler," one Calgary-based trader said.
Temperatures in Calgary are forecast to drop this weekend to a low of -15 degrees Celsius on Sunday, traders said.
One trader said storage may no longer be a factor in the market.

"Even if we withdrew 1.3 bcf (billion cubic feet) out each day through the end of March, we still wouldn't be touching cushion gas," he said, noting that about 800-900 mmcfd of gas was likely withdrawn from storage today.
March AECO prices rose to about C$1.60 per GJ in early trading, but by late morning prices had settled back to the mid-C$1.50s.
April/October AECO was talked at just under C$1.50 per GJ.
At Niagara, prices for Friday were still around $2.10 per mmBtu, while March pricing was at $2.06-2.10, traders said.
